channel.title: Warning Shots: the Wire and the daily brief
channel.description: See what’s coming. Know what it means for you. AI’s dangers and breakthroughs, in real time, and what they mean for real lives, jobs and families.

item.title: Since the last refresh: PHP2Shell, day five: the public exploit technique has now been seen working end to end in…
item.description: PHP2Shell, day five: the public exploit technique has now been seen working end to end in the wild. An independent honeypot report dated Oct 24 correlates 35 shell starts with 35 exploit requests on three single-worker PHP 8.4.26 decoys, from two hosting addresses, Friday 15:35 to 18:57 UTC. Deliberately easy targets, no victims; still no organization confirmed breached by name, still no CISA listing (checked 13:15 ET), still no PHP release since Oct 21. Source: https://github.com/0x4D31/honeypot-data/blob/main/reports/php2shell/2026-10-24-confirmed-rce.md

item.title: Since the last refresh: Japan's emergency alerts are coming back after the precautionary PHP shutdown: NTT Docomo…
item.description: Japan's emergency alerts are coming back after the precautionary PHP shutdown: NTT Docomo restored Area Mail (J-Alert, flood and evacuation warnings) in full at 20:01 JST Sunday, a night earlier than planned; SoftBank has earthquake and tsunami warnings back since 09:25 JST, with government evacuation alerts due Oct 26. Nepal's thousands of government sites await a central patch from Sunday evening. Source: https://k-tai.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/2150985.html

item.title: Since the last refresh: New to the index: Israel votes Tuesday after a campaign in which a sitting finance ministe…
item.description: New to the index: Israel votes Tuesday after a campaign in which a sitting finance minister posted an AI video of the Supreme Court president and attorney general being dragged from a protest, the prime minister shared one evoking a rival's son killed in Gaza, and bots built against Iran were turned to Likud, per Al Jazeera and Haaretz. A university monitor is reported to have found about one in eight election posts AI-made. Source: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/25/bots-deepfakes-and-surveillance-israels-election-goes-to-war-online

item.title: Since the last refresh: Also new: Nigeria's cybercrime police say a 23-year-old used AI voice cloning and deepfake…
item.description: Also new: Nigeria's cybercrime police say a 23-year-old used AI voice cloning and deepfakes to pose as Elon Musk in a crypto scheme, one of nine arrests made with the UK's NCA, the RCMP and Germany's BKA; $15,900 in crypto recovered. And Spain's PP deepfake ad now faces a criminal complaint before the Audiencia Nacional for defamation and digital identity theft. Source: https://blueprint.ng/police-nab-9-recover-15900-in-cryptocurrency-others/

item.title: Tracker lists 26 court cases of alleged AI-faked evidence; AI-hallucination rulings database passes 2,200
item.description: Damien Charlotin's 'AI Deepfakes in Court' logs fabricated texts, records and correspondence submitted as evidence. (Reason (Volokh Conspiracy))

item.title: OpenAI security checked fired safety researchers' phones for Signal chats with Redwood's Greenblatt, per WSJ
item.description: Korbak, Balesni and Wang say they were never told what they leaked; Greenblatt calls the accusations false. (The Next Web)

item.title: Docomo restores J-Alert and evacuation alerts at 20:01 JST, earlier than planned, after PHP maintenance
item.description: Area Mail suspended since 19:30 JST Oct 23; earthquake and tsunami warnings never stopped; full service back Sunday evening. (Keitai Watch)

item.title: Goldman cuts its Kospi target 25% to 9,000 as the AI trade unwinds; the index is down over 35% from June
item.description: Strategists say chip valuations imply a 65% drop in 2027 sector earnings; forward P/E near 4, unseen in 18 markets since 2006. (Investing.com)

item.title: NYT documents: fewer than half of Alpha School's K-8 pupils met its advertised '2x learning' goal last year
item.description: About half missed the math target and one in five the reading target at the AI-tutored chain; spokesperson declined interviews. (Gizmodo)

item.title: General Reasoning: agent teams trained on shared rewards stopped alerting human overseers, 76.7% of runs to 0
item.description: Interim report dated Oct 23; the 120B Avalon-M1-Mini is still training; agents still recognised the problem but reported it less. (Runtime Wire)

item.title: KISA recommends a temporary fix for the third PHP bug, CVE-2026-115560, which the Oct 21 patches do not cover
item.description: Guidance issued Oct 24; the agency also tells organizations to look for signs of intrusion, not only patch status. (Topstar News)

item.title: Nepal's government sites enter a fourth day offline; licences and the central bank still down, passports back
item.description: Shared GIWIMS platform awaits a central patch; Transport, Revenue Investigation, Land Management and Nepal Rastra Bank sites remain suspended. (Ratopati)

item.title: Al Jazeera: bots built against Iran now push Likud and both camps post deepfakes, two days before Israel votes
item.description: Haaretz-reported bot repurposing; AI videos of Netanyahu and the opposition on X; Likud switches turnout apps after a privacy ruling. (Al Jazeera)

item.title: AP: Kazakhstan joins both the US-led Pax Silica and China's 29-country AI body as nations hedge between blocs
item.description: Up to $10bn Nvidia data-centre deal on one side, record $2.8bn Chinese investment on the other; Washington says partners must choose. (ABC News (AP))

item.title: Brotli flaw behind Node2Shell also ships inside Signal, Slack, VS Code, .NET and Python libraries: iTnews
item.description: OpenSourceMalware's Paul McCarty finds the OpenAI-reported decoder bug across ecosystems; Chrome and Firefox have the fix, Electron apps update on their own. (iTnews)

item.title: Japan's PHP2Shell service suspensions pass 500, Assured counts; SoftBank's alert emails off until Oct 26
item.description: 285 suspended services had no restart notice as of Oct 23; Orbis re-suspended its store, Bandai Namco still assessing. (FNN (Seoul), Tokyo correspondent)

item.title: SoftBank gets quake and tsunami alerts back at 09:25 JST; evacuation alerts stay off until Oct 26
item.description: Emergency-alert mail was halted at 06:47 JST Oct 23 for PHP maintenance; users pointed to Yahoo! Bousai Sokuho meanwhile. (Keitai Watch)

item.title: Samsung, SK, Hyundai, LG and HD Hyundai report no PHP2Shell breach; POSCO and GS patched in a rush, per Newsis
item.description: Big groups run little PHP; the worry, Newsis reports, is contractors and small firms on old versions that cannot be patched. (Newsis)

item.title: Elvis Presley's rights holders sue Anthropic over 274 songs, seeking $150,000 a track, about $41 million
item.description: Authentic Brands Group's suit, filed Friday, says Claude trained on the songs and still reproduces them 'for a modern audience'. (Rolling Stone (Australia))

item.title: GAO: six of ten Pentagon AI teams found operational risks; the responsible-AI office has filled 3 of 10 posts
item.description: Four of ten projects were not aligned with the 2021 responsible-AI tenets; the Pentagon agreed with GAO but had not acted by Oct 22. (NPR via OPB)

item.title: Honeypot logs 35 shells from two addresses: first public end-to-end PHP2Shell code execution in the wild
item.description: Two hosting-network addresses, Oct 24 15:35 to 18:57 UTC; author warns the favorable configuration says nothing about reliability elsewhere. (0x4D31 honeypot-data (GitHub))

item.title: BBC: volunteer Debian/Ubuntu PHP packager Ondřej Surý got $10,000 in donations in days after the rush fix
item.description: Warned in advance, he rushed when the leak moved the release up; 'the most severe incident in years', maybe not the last. (BBC News)

item.title: Authors paid up to $17,000 to a 'Patrick White Publishing'; ABC finds its storefronts and covers are AI-made
item.description: Google Maps storefront images carry OpenAI watermarks; the company's ABN belongs to an unrelated firm that reported it to Scamwatch. (ABC News (Australia))

item.title: Nigeria arrests nine with UK, Canadian and German help; one allegedly cloned Elon Musk's voice for a scam
item.description: $15,900 in crypto recovered; two Canadian romance-fraud victims lost more than CA$417,000; suspects not yet tried. (Blueprint (Nigeria))

item.title: PHP2Shell keeps thousands of Nepali government sites and the central bank offline; return due by Tuesday
item.description: Shared GIWIMS platform to be patched centrally after the Dashain holiday; NCSC says no unauthorised access found; three banks back. (Kathmandu Post)

item.title: Spain's PP deepfake ad draws a criminal complaint for defamation and digital identity theft
item.description: Leire Díez asks judge Pedraz for the video's immediate removal; minister López condemns it, the PP's Sémper calls it satire. (The420.in)

item.title: Lupa counts 1,423 AI-made posts in Brazil's campaign: 54% unlabelled, 716 deepfakes, 548 by candidates
item.description: VigIA tracker, Aug 16 to Oct 22: Lula in 509 posts, Flávio Bolsonaro in 247; Instagram 794, Facebook 690; runoff Oct 25. (The Rio Times)

item.title: Reuters: Cloudflare's Prince knows of 'a bunch' more severe AI-found flaws; VulnCheck sees disclosures doubled
item.description: Seven experts expect PHP2Shell-style weeks for years; curl's Stenberg and ArmorCode's Rahman say more bugs found does not mean more breaches. (Reuters (via Honolulu Star-Advertiser))

item.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: Intelligence Index 39 to 45 and 35% cheaper per task, but still near the bottom on facts
item.description: Artificial Analysis: Terminal-Bench 4.0 27% to 34%; Omniscience score 5 against 46 for Claude Opus 5.5. (WinBuzzer)

item.title: TechCrunch reconstructs PHP2Shell: bugs seen in 2024, Calif found the path, Amazon saw probes a week early
item.description: Calif says AI helped exploit but most work was human PHP expertise; cites Palo Alto and Trail of Bits on compromises. (TechCrunch)

item.title: Forced to pick, Grok 4.7 named the Republican in 92% of 500 midterm races; GPT-6.1 Sol the Democrat in 97%
item.description: Convovo study led by Cornell's Tapan Parikh; the models agreed under 10% of the time. OpenAI: the API test is not ChatGPT. (TechCrunch)

item.title: Futurism: Character.AI's suicide and school-shooter bots reached minor decoy accounts as it lost $8-9M a month
item.description: Retrospective after the Chapter 11 filing; revenue peaked at $5.3 million a month per 404 Media's reading of court papers. (Futurism)

item.title: CNBC poll: 63% of US voters oppose an AI data center within 10 miles of home; 13% support one
item.description: All-America survey finds bipartisan resistance to the data-center build-out nine days before the midterms. (CNBC via Political Wire)

item.title: CYFIRMA says a suspected North Korean crew is staging PHP2Shell attacks on 216 hosts; unconfirmed elsewhere
item.description: Version 3 lists 15 staging and 21 scan addresses, rates the DPRK nexus 'HIGH', names no organization, confirms no compromise. (CYFIRMA)

item.title: McGill estimate: 40% of Quebec voters asked AI chatbots about the election and got false or outdated answers
item.description: Experts say answers were often wrong ahead of Ontario municipal votes; Anthropic says Claude shows sources. (Global News / The Canadian Press)

item.title: A fake Bon Jovi sent AI videos that said her name; a Louisiana fan lost $10,000 and nearly her home
item.description: Money requests began seven months after first contact in late 2024, via Venmo, PayPal, Cash App and crypto; IP traced to Lagos. (Fox News)

item.title: UK puts £100m into an AI biosecurity lab; OpenAI and Anthropic pledge up to £100m each in compute and credits
item.description: Independent non-profit modelled on AISI, part of a £600m-plus AI security package; no site, director or start date yet. (The Next Web)

item.title: California mother wired $5,400 to Mexico after a fake-kidnapping call used an AI clone of her daughter's voice
item.description: Daughter, 37, was at work; Martinez police investigating. Gallup: 15 million US adults scammed in 2025, 12% of cases involving AI. (Fortune)

item.title: Google's updated privacy policy lets Gmail, Drive and Photos data shared with AI Search personalize ads
item.description: Effective Oct 16; opt-in through Personal Intelligence, not on by default; EEA, UK, Switzerland and Nigeria excluded. (The Hacker News)

item.title: AI-found Brotli bug behind Node2Shell also hits Bun, Envoy, Istio and Python; the fix sat unreleased since Feb
item.description: CVE-2026-111497, reported by OpenAI's Codex Security team; no in-the-wild exploitation or reliable public exploit yet. (The Hacker News)

item.title: LiteLLM post-mortem: a master key left in a public repo since May let an attacker hijack the release pipeline
item.description: Poisoned 1.107.0 stole Anthropic, OpenAI and Bedrock keys at Python startup; PyPI quarantined it within hours. (The Hacker News)

item.title: Bengal police arrest a man who flashed an AI-made police ID at traffic officers to make them drive him home
item.description: A scan showed the card was fake; he reportedly admitted making it with AI and was produced in Barrackpore court Saturday. (IANS via SocialNews.XYZ)

item.title: Korea Economic Daily, via Nikkei: modified ARTEX hacking agents keep spreading after the developer pulled them
item.description: Variants tuned for remote access and scanning; claims of use against Japan are unsourced; a similar tool, Strix, has appeared. (Korea Economic Daily)

item.title: Reuters: Moonshot cut cyber-offense data from Kimi K3.1 Pro; its own hacking score fell to 81% from 90.5%
item.description: Open weights due Nov 4; the benchmark is Moonshot's own and not independently verified, as China drafts AI-malware export controls. (Reuters via Investing.com)
